newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tiasa gets okay for timber acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Tiasa gets okay for timber acquisitions.

text.p: Malaysian timber products firm Jaya Tiasa Holdings Bhd said on Monday it has received regulatory approval to buy 11 timber concessions and two new timber licences at a revised price of 388.9 million ringgit.
It also received approval from the Securities Commission for a restricted share issue and to rescind a log supply agreement, the company said in a statement released by its merchant bankers.
Jaya Tiasa said it would issue 20.54 million new shares at 11.50 ringgit each and another 152.6 million ringgit to pay for the timber acquisitions.
The company had previously proposed to pay 576.1 million ringgit for the acquisitions by issuing 45.58 million new shares at 8.0 ringgit each and a further 211.46 million ringgit in cash.
Jaya Tiasa said it plans to make a restricted issue of 13.27 million new shares at 11.50 ringgit a share, revised from an earlier plan to issue 26.43 million new shares at 8.0 ringgit each.
A log supply agreement with Rimbunan Hijau Sdn Bhd and wholly-owned Jaya Tiasa Plywood Sdn Bhd will also be rescinded. said Jaya Tiasa.
The Security Commission's approval is subject to the company using proceeds from the restricted issue to part finance the proposed timber concessions.
All vendors of the 11 timber concessions would also have to guarantee 100 percent of maintainable profit before taxation of the concessions for three financial years, said Jaya Tiasa.
The supply agreement rescission will only be effected with the completion of acqusition of at least six timber licencee companies, the statement said.
Jaya Tiasa stock was suspended from Friday, being last traded at 11.80.
